content.user_title: Plan Newsletter Revenue and Sponsorship Pricing
content.value_statement: Newsletter owners often lack a clear link between audience data, pricing, and revenue. This skill builds labeled subscription, sponsorship, and growth scenarios.
actual_capabilities: Models monthly and annual paid-subscription revenue from audience size, conversion assumptions, and tier prices.
Builds sponsorship rate cards using CPM, click-based, or flat-per-send pricing.
Defines advertising inventory, fill-rate assumptions, placement options, and floor prices.
Compares paid-only, sponsorship-only, and hybrid monetization scenarios.
Projects revenue at audience-growth milestones using referral, recommendation, or boost assumptions.
Labels evidence quality and checks sponsorship disclosures, consent gaps, and unsupported claims.
limitations: It does not provide built-in industry benchmarks for conversion rates, CPMs, or referral performance.
It does not connect to email, analytics, ecommerce, or advertising platforms without separate integrations.
It does not calculate final ROI, payback, revenue per send, or list valuation.
Forecasts depend on user data and stated assumptions, so they are not guaranteed outcomes.

use_cases.title: Launch a paid newsletter tier
use_cases.description: Estimate subscriber conversion, monthly revenue, and annual revenue for proposed membership prices.

use_cases.title: Create a sponsorship rate card
use_cases.description: Price placements from active audience, open rates, inventory, cadence, and expected fill rates.

use_cases.title: Compare monetization strategies
use_cases.description: Evaluate paid-only and hybrid plans across audience-growth milestones with explicit assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate paid subscription revenue
prompt_templates.prompt: Model a paid tier for [active subscribers] subscribers at [monthly price]. Use [conversion rate] as an estimate. Show monthly and annual revenue.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner forecast with known audience, price, and conversion inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a sponsorship rate card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sponsorship rate card for [active subscribers] subscribers and [open rate] opens. Compare CPM and flat-per-send pricing. Label every assumption.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate pricing exercise for newsletter advertising inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Compare paid and hybrid plans
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare paid-only and hybrid monetization for my newsletter. Use my [audience metrics], [tier prices], [send cadence], and [sponsor assumptions]. Flag missing inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed strategy comparison across multiple revenue lines.

prompt_templates.title: Model growth, revenue, and compliance
prompt_templates.prompt: Project revenue at current audience, 25 percent growth, and 50 percent growth. Include referral assumptions, sponsorship disclosures, consent gaps, and unsupported claim checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with growth loops, evidence labels, and compliance checks.

output_examples.input: Model a 20,000-subscriber newsletter with a 3 percent paid conversion rate and an 8 dollar monthly tier.
output: Monthly recurring revenue: 4,800 dollars, before fees and churn.
Annual recurring revenue: 57,600 dollars, assuming stable membership.
Open loop: add churn and payment-fee assumptions.

output_examples.input: Create a sponsorship plan for 45,000 active subscribers, a 42 percent open rate, and four monthly sends.
output: Rate card compares CPM pricing with a flat placement price.
Monthly forecast states inventory and fill-rate assumptions.
Checklist requires clear advertising disclosure and supported performance claims.

best_practices: Provide active-subscriber counts, engagement rates, send cadence, prices, and current revenue when available.
Separate measured values from user-provided inputs and estimated assumptions.
Test conservative, expected, and ambitious scenarios before selecting prices or inventory.
anti_patterns: Do not present assumed conversion rates or fill rates as measured results.
Do not include subscribers who lack consent for commercial messages.
Do not promise revenue outcomes or use unsupported sponsor performance claims.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide active subscribers, open and click rates, send cadence, monetization goals, proposed prices, and any current revenue.

faq.question: Can it create a sponsorship rate card?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare CPM, click-based, and flat-per-send pricing with inventory and fill-rate assumptions.

faq.question: Does it include industry benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. Missing benchmarks remain labeled as estimates or marked as needing a source.

faq.question: Can it model several paid tiers?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide each tier price and conversion assumption so the model can calculate separate revenue lines.

faq.question: Does it connect to my email platform?
faq.answer: Not by default. You can provide exports or use a separately configured connector for supported platforms.

faq.question: Does it calculate newsletter ROI?
faq.answer: No. It prepares revenue inputs and projections, but a separate ROI tool should calculate payback and list value.
